questions.question: The total surface area of a solid right circular cylinder of height 13 cm, is 880 cm². Its volume (in cm³) is 11k, The value of k is: (take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total surface area of solid right circular cylinder = 880 cm2

Height of the right circular cylinder = 13 cm 

**Formulas used:**

Total surface area of a cylinder = 2πrh + 2πr²

Volume of the cylinder = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad73dbaaf925fea38524c2b9dd5814bba718006d60c8ede2aae37815e7ee5823.png] 

Total surface area of right circular cylinder = 880 cm²

⇒ 2πrh + 2πr2 = 880

⇒ 2πr(h + r) = 880 

⇒ 2 × 22/7 × r × (13 + r) = 880 

⇒ (13 + r)r = 880 × 7/22 × 1/2

⇒ 13r + r² = 140

⇒ r2 + 13r - 140 = 0

⇒ r2 + 20r - 7r - 140 = 0

⇒ r(r + 20) - 7(r + 20) = 0

⇒ (r - 7)(r + 20) = 0

⇒ r = 7, r ≠ 20

Volume of the right circular cylinder = 11k 

⇒ 22/7 × 7 × 7 × 13 = 11k 

⇒ 22/7 × 7 × 7 × 13 × 1/11 = k

⇒ k = 182 

**∴ The required value of k is 182.**

questions.question: A person saves 28% of his income. If his income increases by 20% and the expenditure reduces by 5%, then his savings increase by x%. The value of x is closest to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net change in **Income** = Net change in **Savings** + Net change in **Expenditure**.

Decrease in **Expenditure** = 5% of (100 − 28) = 5% of 72 = 3.6.

Growth required in **Savings** = 20 (Income rise) + 3.6 (Exp reduction) = 23.6.

Percentage **Savings** increase = (23.6 ÷ 28) × 100 ≈ 84.3%.

The closest value in the given options is 84.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 84.5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Savings** = 28% of **Income**

**Income** increase = 20%

**Expenditure** decrease = 5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/daf58d37b37076a42bc0361580ff432311c3189a9ff6916aefa9b7a1e991a152.png] 

Let the initial **Income** be 100.

⇒ **Savings** = 28

⇒ **Expenditure** = 100 − 28 = 72

⇒ New **Income** = 100 + (20% of 100) = 120

⇒ New **Expenditure** = 72 − (5% of 72) = 72 − 3.6 = 68.4

⇒ New **Savings** = New **Income** − New **Expenditure** = 120 − 68.4 = 51.6

⇒ Increase in **Savings** = 51.6 − 28 = 23.6

⇒ Percentage increase (x) = (23.6 ÷ 28) × 100

⇒ x = 84.2857...

⇒ Value closest to x = 84.5

**∴ The correct answer is 84.5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Income Components

The fundamental relation is **Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**. Any change in **Income** must be balanced by the sum of changes in **Expenditure** and **Savings**.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Increase/Decrease = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

Successive Change Principle

When calculating changes on components (like expenditure), always calculate the percentage change based on their specific base values, not the total income base unless specified.</p

questions.question:
What is the mean of the median and the mode of the data:

19, 20, 14, 15, 19, 16, 17, 15,14, 13, 18, 19, 17, 13
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange data in **ascending order**: 13, 13, 14, 14, 15, 15, 16, 17, 17, 18, 19, 19, 19, 20.

**Mode** (value with highest frequency) = 19 (appears 3 times).

**Median** (average of 7th and 8th terms for n=14) = (16 + 17) ÷ 2 = 16.5.

Required **Mean** = (16.5 + 19) ÷ 2 = 35.5 ÷ 2 = 17.75.

**∴ The correct answer is 17.75.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given data:** 19, 20, 14, 15, 19, 16, 17, 15, 14, 13, 18, 19, 17, 13

**Step 1:** Count the total number of observations (n).

⇒ n = 14

**Step 2:** Arrange observations in **ascending order** to find the median.

⇒ 13, 13, 14, 14, 15, 15, 16, 17, 17, 18, 19, 19, 19, 20

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38d2b0d8db586571b212a4948c0c7f62446f3a5d1b34cad8c34a348964fb0208.png] 

**Step 3:** Calculate the **Median**.

⇒ Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Median = [7th term + 8th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Median = (16 + 17) ÷ 2 = 16.5

**Step 4:** Calculate the **Mode**.

⇒ Frequency of 19 is 3 (maximum).

⇒ Mode = 19

**Step 5:** Calculate the **Mean** of Median and Mode.

⇒ Mean = (Median + Mode) ÷ 2

⇒ Mean = (16.5 + 19) ÷ 2 = 35.5 ÷ 2 = 17.75

**∴ The correct answer is 17.75.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even and Odd Data

For odd n, Median = ((n+1)/2)th term. For even n, Median = average of (n/2)th and (n/2+1)th terms.

Empirical Relationship

The relation between mean, median, and mode is given by: **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**.

Mode Definition

The **Mode** is the observation that occurs most frequently in the data set. A set can be unimodal, bimodal, or multimodal.</p

__
 
• **Osteoporosis**__

 __
 
• **Osteoclasts** are the** cells that degrade bone to initiate normal bone remodeling and mediate bone loss in pathologic conditions by increasing their resorptive activity.**
 
• They are derived from precursors in the myeloid/monocyte lineage that circulate in the blood after their formation in the bone marrow.
 
• **Osteoporosis **increases the size of these spaces, causing the bone to lose strength and density.
 
• It is often called a silent disease because a person cannot feel the weakening of the bones.
 
• Breaking a bone is often the first sign of osteoporosis.
 
• The most common drugs used to treat osteoporosis are called bisphosphonates.
 
• They help to prevent the loss of bone mass and can be taken orally or by injection.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acromegaly**__

 __
 
• A disorder in adults in which the pituitary gland produces too much growth hormone.
 
• Acromegaly is usually caused by a non-cancerous tumor. 
 
• Middle-aged adults are most commonly affected.
 
• Symptoms include enlargement of the face, hands, and feet.
 
 
 
• **Fibrous dysplasia**__
 
 
• Fibrous dysplasia is a disorder where normal bone and marrow are replaced with fibrous tissue, resulting in formation of bone that is weak and prone to expansion.
 
• It is very rare, and there is no known cure. It is not a form of cancer.

questions.question: What does Article 32 of the Indian Constitution deal with?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Constitutional Remedies.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32**__

 __
 
• **Article 32** of the** Indian Constitution** has been described as the** 'heart and soul' of the Indian Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.**
 
• It gives a citizen the right to approach the Supreme Court to get resorted any of the fundamental rights in case of their violation.
 
• It is also known as the Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• Right to move the Supreme court for the enforcement of the writs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Habeas Corpus**__: This writ is issued to produce a person who has been detained whether in prison or in private custody, before a court and to release him if such detention is found illegal.
 
• __**Mandamus**__: The writ of command is issued by the supreme or high court when any government court, corporation, or any public authority has to do a public duty fails to do so.
 
• __**Prohibition**__: It is a writ issued by a higher court directing a lower court or tribunal to refrain from proceeding in a matter over which it has no jurisdiction or authority.
 
• __**Certiorari**__: The writ of certiorari can be issued by the supreme court, tribunal or quasi-judicial authority.
 
• __**Quo-Warranto**__: The writ of quo-warranto can be issued by the supreme or high court for asking of by what authority or warrant. It is issued by the court to enquire into the legality of a claim of a person to a public office.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book ‘Shame’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salman Rushdie.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Book **"Shame"**__

 __
 
• Shame is **Salman Rushdie's third novel.**
 
• It is published in **1983.**
 
• It was written out of a desire to approach the problem of "artificial" country divisions, their residents' complicity, and the problems of post-colonialism.
 
• The book is written in the style of magic realism.
 
• The central theme of the book is that begetting "shame" begets violence.
 
 
 
• **Salman Rushdie**__
 
 
• He is an Indian-born British-American novelist and essayist.
 
• His second novel, **Midnights's Children (1981**), won the **Booker Prize in 1981.**
 
• The Satanic Verses (1988) was the subject of a major controversy, provoking protests from Muslims in several countries.
 
• He has received many plaudits for his writings, including the European Union's Aristeion Prize for Literature, the Premio Grinzane Cavour and the Writer of the Year Award in Germany, and many of literature's highest honours.

questions.question: ______ is caused when a child’s growing bones fail to develop due to a lack of vitamin D.

__
 
• Vitamins__

 __
 
• Vitamins are chemical compounds that are required in small amounts for growth and good health and are obtained from our food.
 
• The vitamins are not synthesized in the body that's why they must be supplied through the diet.
 
 
 
• ​**Vitamin D**__
 __
 
• ​It increases calcium absorption from the gastrointestinal tract and helps to control calcium deposition in the bone.
 
• Its sources are Cod liver oil, skin can synthesize vitamin D in the presence of sunlight.
 
• Its deficiency is Rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• ​Vitamin C__

 
 
• Vitamin C is a water-soluble compound found in living organisms.​
 
• It is an essential nutrient for various metabolism in our body and also serves as a reagent for the preparation of many materials in the pharmaceutical and food industry.
 
• Its deficiency causes **Scurvy.**
 
• Vitamin C also known as ascorbic acid is an essential nutrient in many multicellular organisms, especially in humans.
 
• Ascorbic acid is a water-soluble vitamin and is found in variable quantities in fruits and vegetables and organ meats.
